why_angle: findingtheuniverse.com (cited) says the Peak Design Travel Tripod's head can't be swapped and calls its plate proprietary, and digitalnomads.world (cited) names no adapter. This page sources Peak Design's $29.95 Universal Head Adapter, Shutter Muse's tests of Arca plates in the stock clamp, Ulanzi's own note that the Zero Y head is not detachable, and Camera Jabber on the Sirui 5C's screw-off head. The column-down height angle (A/B) was not used because Sirui publishes no column-down height for the 5C and retailers disagree on it.

page.title: Best Travel Tripod for Camera (2026): Head Swaps, Load and Packed Size Compared
page.h1: Travel tripod for camera: which one packs small and lets you change the head
page.desc: Lightweight travel camera tripods from Peak Design, Ulanzi and Sirui compared on head swaps, Arca plate clamps, rated load, folded length, weight and price.
page.answer: Short answer. The best travel tripod for a camera is the Peak Design Travel Tripod (aluminum): it packs to 39.1 cm, holds 9.1 kg, and its ball head swaps for any standard head with a $29.95 adapter. The lightweight Ulanzi Zero Y head is fixed; the Sirui Traveler 5C is the 0.85 kg budget pick.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Carbon saves 0.27 kg for $200. 1.56 kg − 1.29 kg = 0.27 kg (Peak Design's figures); $599.95 − $399.95 = $200, about $741 per kg saved.
  • The Sirui folds 6.1 cm shorter than the Peak Design. 39.1 cm − 33 cm = 6.1 cm. The Ulanzi Zero Y is 42.3 − 39.1 = 3.2 cm longer than the Peak Design.
  • The Peak Design is rated for 2.3× the Sirui's load. 9.1 kg ÷ 4 kg = 2.3. The Zero Y's ball head is rated 5 kg (Ridgeline Images).
  • A new head costs 7.5% more, not a second tripod. $29.95 ÷ $399.95 = 7.5% on top of the aluminum Peak Design.
  • Stability. TechGearLab scored the aluminum Peak Design 7.0 and the Sirui Traveler 5C 5.0 for stability; Zach Lovell found the Sirui's centre column wobbly when fully extended.

Can you change the head later?

The head is the part travel shooters most often outgrow: video needs a fluid pan head, and panoramas need a levelling base. Here is what each tripod allows.

  • Peak Design Travel Tripod: yes, two ways. Peak Design's $29.95 Universal Head Adapter replaces the built-in Compact Ball Head, which comes off with the included hex wrench. The adapter takes "any standard 3rd party tripod head" and fits both the carbon and aluminum versions, with or without the center column. For an occasional second head, keep the stock clamp instead. Dan Carr of Shutter Muse mounted an RRS BH-55 and an Acratech GXP by fitting an Arca-Swiss plate under each head. He reports the clamp takes other Arca plates and L-brackets once its two stopper screws are removed; with the screws in, only Peak Design's plate fits. Peak Design's Standard Plate ($19.95 on its own) "works with most ARCA-type tripods".
  • Ulanzi Zero Y: only with an extra part. Ulanzi's store page says "The tripod ball head is not detachable" and recommends its F38 1/4 center column for anyone who wants a different head. David Lowe (Ridgeline Images) confirms the clamp is Arca-Swiss compatible but found the head "tends to sag under heavy loads".
  • Sirui Traveler 5C: yes. Camera Jabber found that the centre column unscrews and a head screws straight onto the crown in about a minute; the base plate is Arca Swiss-style. {buy:sirui-traveler-5c-carbon-travel-tripod}
  • Already own Manfrotto plates? On the Manfrotto Befree Advanced AS (twist lock, aluminum), the Arca-type plate holder also works with Manfrotto's RC2 system, according to Manfrotto. It has a 3/8" top thread and a 9 kg safety payload rated to UNI/PdR 105:2021, and it weighs 1.51 kg and closes to 40 cm.
